title: Translate region outage lessons into verifiable model-routing contracts
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Convert the action items from the 2026-02-22 regional outage postmortem into concrete PRD requirements: explicit model-routing contracts, graded fallback tiers, verification gates, and observability updates that can be validated during release. The goal is to ensure predictable behavior during partial-region failures and to give operators clear, testable rollbacks and fallback behaviors.
background: On 2026-02-22 a partial region outage exposed gaps in our automatic routing and fallback logic: warm pool warmups were delayed, KV cache regeneration caused token amplification, and runtime routing fallbacks sometimes selected incompatible model variants leading to degraded outputs. The postmortem enumerated action items (see links) and recommended product requirements. This ticket translates those actions into scope, acceptance criteria, and rollout/verification steps for the serving runtime PRD.
incident_summary: Region us-west-2 lost partial capacity for 27 minutes. Primary symptoms: increased cold-start latency, KV cache misses causing request retries, and routing decisions that sent traffic to a model variant without required tokenizer compatibility. Customer impact: several latency-sensitive endpoints exceeded SLOs; documented in postmortem.
postmortem_actions: Define deterministic routing contracts for region vs. tier vs. model-compatibility
Introduce graded fallback tiers: local-region degraded, cross-region warmed, degraded-light, best-effort (quantized)
Ensure tokenizer/format compatibility checks are part of fallback selection
Add KV cache regeneration rate limiters and backpressure signals to autoscaler
Add synthetic canary traffic and runtime invariants to detect incorrect fallbacks
Document on-call playbook updates and rollback runbooks tied to routing contract violations
prd_changes_required: Routing contract: explicit policy document stating priority rules (region, tier, latency, compatibility). This must be machine-readable and versioned.
Fallback definitions: enumerated tiers with deterministic selection logic and max acceptable quality delta per tier.
Compatibility matrix: model variant -> tokenizer + quantization compatibility table that routing checks before selecting fallback.
Throttle/regen controls: config knobs for KV cache regen rate, global and per-customer backpressure thresholds.
Observability hooks: per-request routing decision traces, fallback reason codes, and synthetic canary dashboards.
Release gates: automated verification steps that must pass before cross-region traffic ramp (synthetic traffic, trace sampling, and output-quality checks).
acceptance_criteria: Machine-readable routing contract exists in repo and is loaded by the control plane (PR + unit tests present)
Fallback selection deterministic: given the same inputs and simulated region-loss, recorded routing decisions must match expected fallback tier (automated integration test)
Compatibility checks prevent incompatible model variant selection in 100% of simulated fallback cases (test harness)
KV cache regen limiter reduces regen-induced QPS amplification by >= 60% in stress tests compared to current baseline
Synthetic canary suite detects incorrect fallback selection within 2 minutes of a simulated region loss
Runbook updated and verified by on-call drill: median restored routing within SLA windows and documented operator steps
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): implement machine-readable contract and routing check in the control plane; run full synthetic suite against staging clusters. Phase 2 (pilot): enable on low-traffic customers in us-west-2 with detailed tracing and automated rollback hooks. Phase 3 (gradual ramp): increase region traffic with 4-hour verification windows and automated abort on SLO regressions. Phase 4: global release with updated docs and on-call training.
verification_steps: Run integration test: simulate region loss and assert recorded fallback reason codes match expected matrix
Execute synthetic canary traffic for 30 minutes and verify no false-positive fallbacks
Run KV cache regen stress test and measure regen QPS and downstream request amplification
Manual review of per-request traces for 50 routed requests across fallback tiers
On-call drill: trigger playbook and confirm operator can execute rollback in < 15 minutes
notes: PM/Eng sync 2026-03-03: agreed to prioritize machine-readable contract before fallback plumbing
Design caution: user-facing changes to 'best-effort' tier terminology to be verified with legal for SLA language
Trade-off: stricter compatibility checks may reduce fallback availability; mitigations include pre-warmed cross-region pools and faster KV cache snapshot transfer
